questions.label: 20-21 4(a)
questions.text: The magnetic vector potential of a Hertzian dipole is given by: $\vec{A} = \frac{\mu_0 Idl}{4\pi r}e^{-j\beta r}\hat{z}$. Show that magnetic field, $H = \frac{Idl}{4\pi}\cos(\theta)\left[\frac{j\beta}{r} + \frac{1}{r^2}\right]e^{-j\beta r}\hat{\phi}$  *[sic: should be $\sin(\theta)$]*.
questions.outline: Take the curl of A in spherical coordinates; divide by μ to get H.

questions.label: 20-21 4(b)
questions.text: Using the expression of $H$ found in 4(a), show that the electric field component $E = \frac{\eta Idl}{4\pi}\cos(\theta)\left[\frac{j\beta}{r} + \frac{1}{r^2} - \frac{j}{\beta r^3}\right]e^{-j\beta r}\hat{\theta} + \frac{\eta Idl}{2\pi}\cos(\theta)\left[\frac{1}{r^2} - \frac{j}{\beta r^3}\right]e^{-j\beta r}\hat{r}$  *[sic: the $\hat{\theta}$ term should have $\sin(\theta)$]*
questions.outline: Use the curl of H in free space; divide by jωε; collect the r and θ components of E.

questions.label: 20-21 4(c)
questions.text: Find the expression of average power density of Hertzian dipole in far field zone.
questions.outline: Keep the 1/r far-field terms; form the Poynting vector E × H*; average it over time.
